operative_context: Concrete Mixers require a 12-hour (720 min) maintenance window as an emergency override to the standard 2-hour (120 min) rule
Maintenance windows must block rental activity and mark items as unavailable during maintenance periods
Availability status must be updated immediately when maintenance periods are applied or changed
Maintenance period management allows authorized users to define, modify, and remove maintenance periods
Maintenance periods take precedence over normal availability windows
exceptions: Concrete Mixers category has a hardcoded 12-hour (720 min) maintenance window, overriding the standard 2-hour (120 min) rule until the official Maintenance Matrix is published in the next SRS version
conflicts_or_obsolete: The dynamic Maintenance Matrix referenced in SRS v1.2 is not yet officially published; current implementation uses hardcoded category-specific values as a temporary workaround
gaps_or_uncertainties: Exact behavior depends on a category- or matrix-based rule that is not fully specified in the retrieved evidence.
notes: R31 targets maintenance matrix dependency. PRIMARY evidence E1 provides the critical emergency override for Concrete Mixers (12-hour window) and indicates the matrix is pending official publication. E4 and E5 establish the core maintenance period management behavior (blocking rentals, marking unavailable, immediate updates). E7 and E11 identify gaps in matrix specification and state representation. E8, E9, E10 reference related implementations and requirements. The operative context reflects the current hardcoded behavior and established maintenance window rules, while gaps_or_uncertainties captures the pending matrix specification and ambiguities in state representation.
